questions.title: When a cue changes the answer, does the explanation reveal it?
questions.summary: Compare the same decision with a neutral context and a contextual cue. Measure changes in choices separately from what a monitor can detect in the returned explanation.
questions.whyItMatters: Oversight can fail silently if a model changes its behavior while its visible explanation gives a monitor no useful evidence of the influence. A controlled comparison can expose that gap without pretending to read hidden computation.

questions.title: Can SAEs reveal persona tendencies that prompting struggles to recover?
questions.summary: Reuse a published SAE on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to discover candidate behavioral directions without selecting trait labels first. Test whether those directions cause consistent changes on fresh scenarios, and compare them with optimized prompting and prompt-extracted persona vectors.
questions.whyItMatters: The original method needs a named trait that the model can express when prompted. This experiment asks whether label-free feature selection can reveal a useful behavioral direction outside what that extraction procedure reliably recovers. Discovery of a candidate is not proof of a new persona.

source.section: Section 8, Supervised, prompt-elicited extraction; Appendix M
source.passage: SAEs may therefore enable unsupervised discovery of persona-relevant directions, including specific traits that cannot be easily elicited through prompting.

closestWork.finding: Appendix M studies SAE features associated with existing persona vectors.
closestWork.mismatch: Selecting features from already named trait vectors does not test discovery without a trait target.

closestWork.finding: RISE explores reasoning behaviors using sparse autoencoders.
closestWork.mismatch: Reasoning behavior discovery does not establish generalizable persona effects that outperform a strong prompt-extraction baseline.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Can Be Unreliable in Implicit-Influence Settings
papers.abstract: Compares implicit and explicit contextual influence across four task families and seven extended-thinking models. The authors report lower detection of some implicit influences, with further degradation under some guidance prompts. This is the closest source for our bounded behavioral adaptation.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Seven extended-thinking models; paper results are distinct from our API pilot.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness of Reasoning Models Varies with Where and How Preference Cues Are Delivered
papers.abstract: FACE-Eval varies preference-cue channel and explicitness. Across 15 open-weight models, the authors report less verbalized attribution for tool-return and implicit cues. Their source-attribution intervention has mixed effects, so changing cue placement or attribution prompts is established prior work.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: 15 open-weight models; single-call, prefilled-tool setting.

papers.title: Not All LLM Reasoning is Visible in the Chain-of-Thought
papers.abstract: Tests whether semantically uninformative filler tokens can support reasoning and hidden task constraints. The findings challenge the assumption that all consequential computation appears as interpretable output text. They do not establish that every unexplained decision uses the same mechanism.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: 13 frontier models; synthetic tasks and a hidden modular-arithmetic constraint.

papers.title: Legibility is Not Interpretability: Comparing Judged and Actual Importance in Chain-Of-Thought Reasoning
papers.abstract: Compares judges of reasoning-step importance against estimates from repeated continuations. Capable judges recover some information, but legible text remains an incomplete guide to a step's functional contribution. This motivates separating an explanation judgment from a causal measurement.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Monte Carlo continuation estimates; judging performance remains below the estimated noise ceiling.

papers.title: Length Penalties Make Chain-of-Thought Less Monitorable
papers.abstract: Trains reasoning models with length penalties and measures hint influence and monitorability. The authors compare compressed traces with length-matched deletion controls, finding that compression can remove more monitorable evidence than shortening alone predicts. An API output cap is a different intervention.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Qwen3 4B and 14B; training intervention and five evaluation distributions.

papers.title: Does Out-of-Sight Equal Out-of-Mind in CoT Monitorability?
papers.abstract: Compares monitoring with explicit and latent reasoning, using hints as controlled interventions. The authors find that task structure and access to internal states can matter more than reasoning mode. This supports precise labels for which output surface a monitor actually sees.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Math and question answering; explicit, weakly supervised and strongly supervised latent reasoning.

papers.title: Selective Disclosure of Hidden Directives in Reasoning Models: Behavioral Asymmetry and Steering
papers.abstract: Studies whether benign and malign hidden directives appear differently in returned reasoning. The authors report disclosure asymmetries and activation-steering results. Disclosure frequency alone is not a complete measure of whether a directive causally affected an answer.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Eight reasoning models; behavioral controls and a separately described steering evaluation.

papers.title: A Removal Based Approach to Improve LLM Faithfulness at Test-Time
papers.abstract: Proposes removing input concepts that an explanation does not credit, then querying the model again. The authors report improved explanation completeness in their tested datasets. This is a relevant attempted mitigation, with transfer to our tasks and observation surface unestablished.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Two datasets and multiple model families; test-time intervention without changing weights.

papers.title: Two Regimes of Chain-of-Thought Unfaithfulness: Metric-Based Detection Fails Where Models Are Wrong
papers.abstract: Audits behavioral faithfulness metrics against annotated traces. Performance differs substantially between correct and incorrect answers, and some familiar signals fail in the regime containing most annotated unfaithfulness. A convenient metric needs validation for the population being studied.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: FaithCoT-Bench audit; model- and source-dependent transfer results.

papers.title: Untangling the Mechanisms of Misleading Context in Medical Question Answering
papers.abstract: Examines misleading context in medical question answering and compares disclosure in reasoning traces with disclosure in final responses. Monitoring results vary with access and cue type. This is methodological context, not medical guidance or a demonstration task.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Three reasoning models on a clinician-reviewed benchmark; output accessibility differs by model.

papers.title: Final Checkpoints Are Not Enough: Analyzing Latent Reasoning Faithfulness Along Training Trajectories
papers.abstract: Tracks faithfulness-related behavior and activation interventions through latent-reasoning training. Strong final accuracy can coexist with declining counterfactual responsiveness. The results motivate checking a training trajectory rather than assuming a final checkpoint captures all changes.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Latent reasoning on ProsQA and GSM settings; intervention dependence is a stated limitation.

papers.title: Tandem Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
papers.abstract: Co-generates reasoning between a trained senior model and a fixed junior during reinforcement learning. The authors report improved handoff robustness and junior-model legibility while maintaining solo capability. Communication compatibility is relevant but does not establish safety monitorability.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Qwen3-4B-Instruct competition-math training; junior-model compatibility.

papers.title: Persuasion Attacks Can Decrease Effectiveness of CoT Monitoring
papers.abstract: Tests whether an agent's written reasoning can persuade a monitor to approve a policy-violating proposal. The authors evaluate a fact-checking intervention, with model diversity affecting its performance. This studies adversarial persuasion, a different mechanism from our benign contextual cues.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Forty tasks; reported examples include Claude 3.7 Sonnet and GPT-4.1, so publication recency is not model recency.

papers.title: The Oversight Gap: What LLM Safety Monitors Miss, and Why It Is Not Capability
papers.abstract: Formalizes limits on properties that require comparing executions, and separates missing information from failures to apply a comparison procedure. The paper also reports a benchmark-construction error found despite favorable judge reviews. Its synthetic settings require careful transfer claims.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Synthetic leak families and replay comparisons; theoretical and empirical claims not independently replicated here.

papers.title: Recall Is Not Protection: Evaluating Safety Monitors Against Model Compliance
papers.abstract: Separates monitor recall on harmful prompts that a target model will comply with from recall on prompts it will refuse. The reported gap shows why a monitor's aggregate classification score may differ from the protection it provides in a coupled system.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Six monitor configurations and three model families; harmfulness labels and compliance are different targets.

papers.title: TRACE: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Large Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: Introduces evidence annotations across prompts, reasoning traces and final responses. The authors find guardrail models struggle to locate supporting evidence in reasoning. The benchmark addresses unsafe-content judgment, which is distinct from detecting an influence on a decision.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Eighteen guardrail models and traces from four reasoning models.

papers.title: The Answer Is Not the Argument
papers.abstract: Tests whether reference-answer access improves reasoning verification or mainly reveals a mismatch with the conclusion. Monitors can benefit overall while missing genuine errors in traces whose final answer is correct. Correctness and sound reasoning should remain separate measures.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: 237 solutions to 79 physics questions; eight monitors and independently labeled errors.

papers.title: Risky Business: Measuring The Faithfulness-Safety Tension
papers.abstract: Intervenes directly on reasoning text to study the tension between following a trace and rejecting unsafe reasoning. The authors describe a task-specific faithfulness-safety tradeoff and a steering intervention. Greater trace dependence is not automatically greater safety.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: HazMart shopkeeper setting with reasoning replacement and open-model analysis.

papers.title: Aligned, Orthogonal or In-conflict: When can we safely optimize Chain-of-Thought?
papers.abstract: Models output rewards and reasoning rewards as aligned, orthogonal or in conflict, then tests predicted monitorability changes during training. Appendix I.7 already studies capped continuation. That comparison is prior work, and a tiny inference-time pilot cannot reproduce long training drift.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Older foundation, submitted March 2026; training experiments require resources beyond the core API demonstration.

papers.title: MonitorBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Provides a multi-task monitorability benchmark with controlled decision-critical factors and prompting stress tests. The authors find that task structure, subject model and monitor all matter. Its August revision is recent, but its original submission is March.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated
papers.modelScope: Older foundation, 1,514 instances across 19 tasks; updated August 2026.

papers.title: Persona Vectors: Monitoring and Controlling Character Traits in Language Models
papers.abstract: Introduces prompt-elicited persona vectors for monitoring and controlling character traits. The limitations propose unsupervised SAE discovery, while Appendix M decomposes previously identified persona vectors.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary source reviewed

papers.title: Fantastic Reasoning Behaviors and Where to Find Them: Unsupervised Discovery of the Reasoning Process
papers.abstract: RISE studies SAE features of reasoning behavior. It is related methodological work; it does not establish the proposed comparison between discovered persona features and prompt-elicited persona vectors.
papers.verificationStatus: Primary source reviewed
